solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Emergency road layer ought to put in more granite (4,8)

blocks.note: granite is hard, so more granite is HARDER

annotation.surface: A road builder is told to lay down more granite.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pictures the workman who lays the road; the definition is instead a layer of the road itself, the strip kept for emergencies.
annotation.definitionFit: The hard shoulder is the paved strip beside a motorway where a car may stop in an emergency.

entries.clue: The short brush enters up most piping (7)

indicatorNotes.short: THE cut short loses its last letter
indicatorNotes.enters: to enter is to go into something, so SET-TO goes into TH
indicatorNotes.up: in a down clue, up reverses the whole assembly

blocks.note: a brush is a short fight, a set-to

annotation.surface: A chimney sweep's brush is pushed up into a very hot flue.
annotation.walkthrough: Piping here is the adjective, as in piping hot, so most piping is the hottest.
annotation.definitionFit: Piping hot means very hot, so the most piping is the hottest.

entries.clue: Order to dispel mob’s former capital judgment (4,3)

blocks.note: Rio de Janeiro was Brazil's capital until 1960
tact = good judgment in dealing with people

annotation.surface: A crowd's former capital punishment, as if a mob once passed death sentences.
annotation.walkthrough: Capital judgment reads as a death sentence, but the phrase splits: capital goes with former, and judgment stands alone.
annotation.definitionFit: The Riot Act was the British law read aloud to order an unruly crowd to disperse.

entries.clue: Odd selection of sayings encapsulating these collected works? (9)

indicatorNotes.Odd selection of: take the odd-numbered letters of SAYINGS

annotation.surface: An anthology of proverbs, an odd selection of sayings, sits within someone's collected works.
annotation.walkthrough: Collected works suggests an author's complete output; the question mark warns it means things put together, which is what a synthesis is.
annotation.definitionFit: A synthesis is a combination of parts into a whole, so syntheses are works of collecting together.

entries.clue: Old hit for Rolling Stones (5)

indicatorNotes.Rolling: rolling over turns SLAP back to front

annotation.surface: An old hit record by the Rolling Stones.
annotation.walkthrough: The band's name is split: Rolling works on hit, and Stones alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain example: the opal is a gemstone prized for its shifting play of colours.

entries.clue: Scaly river beast rearing up (7)

indicatorNotes.rearing up: in a down clue, rearing up turns the letters upside down

annotation.surface: A scaly creature, perhaps a crocodile, rises up out of a river.
annotation.walkthrough: Scaly reads as the beast's skin, but it is the definition: made of thin flakes or layers.
annotation.definitionFit: Laminar means arranged in thin layers or plates, like scales.

entries.clue: Half-worn flea collar retaining medium protection on one side (7)

indicatorNotes.Half-worn: FLEA is worn down to half its letters
indicatorNotes.retaining: to retain is to keep hold of, so RUFF keeps M held inside it

blocks.note: a ruff is a frilled collar
m = medium, as on clothing labels

annotation.surface: A pet's flea collar, half worn out, still has some protective medicine in it.
annotation.walkthrough: The flea collar invites a pet scene; the definition is cryptic, since each earmuff guards one side of the head.
annotation.definitionFit: An earmuff is a pad that protects one ear from cold, one side of the head.

entries.clue: Bucks and more in company releases (4,8)

annotation.surface: A firm releasing dollars and more, as in a company paying out bucks.
annotation.walkthrough: Bucks looks like dollars; it is Buckinghamshire, one of the Home Counties, the counties surrounding London.
annotation.definitionFit: Buckinghamshire (Bucks) is one of the Home Counties that ring London, so Bucks and more are the Home Counties.

entries.clue: Couple bunging old vase no longer of use (7)

indicatorNotes.bunging: to bung something is to shove it in: TWO goes into URN

annotation.surface: Two people throw out an old vase they no longer use.
annotation.walkthrough: Bunging reads as throwing away; in the wordplay it means stuffing something in, as you bung things into a bag.
annotation.definitionFit: Something outworn is worn out and no longer serviceable.

entries.clue: Approved of plug diameter on sink in Slough (7)

indicatorNotes.on: D is set next to MIRE, following it

blocks.note: to plug a product is to advertise it; an ad
to mire is to sink in a slough, a bog

annotation.surface: Someone praises a sink plug of the right width, fitted in Slough.
annotation.walkthrough: Slough is capitalised to look like the English town west of London; here it is a swamp, and to mire is to sink in one.
annotation.definitionFit: To admire is to regard with approval.

entries.clue: Licensed bar limits salted nuts and charcuterie (12)

indicatorNotes.bar limits: LICENSED is barred its outer letters, L and D
indicatorNotes.nuts: nuts = crazy, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: LICENSED without its first and last letters

annotation.surface: A pub serving salted nuts and cold meats as bar snacks.
annotation.walkthrough: Salted nuts look like a bar snack; nuts is the anagram signal and salted is fodder. Limits are the outer letters of the word before bar.
annotation.definitionFit: Charcuterie is both cured meats and the shop that sells them, a delicatessen.

entries.clue: Two types of wood on European bunk (7)

indicatorNotes.on: the woods are placed after E

annotation.surface: A European bunk bed made of two different woods.
annotation.walkthrough: Bunk looks like a bed; it is the definition in the sense of nonsense.
annotation.definitionFit: Bunk and eyewash both mean nonsense or humbug.

entries.clue: Animal barking unless holding its lead (7)

indicatorNotes.barking: barking = mad, so UNLESS is scrambled
indicatorNotes.holding: the scrambled letters hold A inside
indicatorNotes.lead: the lead of ANIMAL is its first letter

annotation.surface: A dog that barks unless someone is holding its lead.
annotation.walkthrough: Animal looks like the dog; it is an adjective, as in animal passions, meaning physical or carnal.
annotation.definitionFit: Animal as an adjective means of the body, fleshly, which is sensual.

entries.clue: Music group centre to concoct etudes (5)

indicatorNotes.centre to: the answer sits in the middle of the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the join of the two words, from the tail of the first into the head of the second

annotation.surface: A band's central figure composes studies for them to play.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer straddles concoct and etudes. Etudes are musical studies, which keeps the whole scene musical.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: octet names any ensemble of eight players, as quartet names four.

entries.clue: Sleepy from poor sci-fi novel (9)

indicatorNotes.novel: novel = new, so the letters are rearranged into a new form

annotation.surface: A reader nodding off over a badly written science-fiction book.
annotation.walkthrough: Novel sits naturally after sci-fi as the book, but it signals the rearrangement. Sleepy here means sleep-inducing, as a dull book is.
annotation.definitionFit: Soporific means inducing sleep, or drowsy.

entries.clue: Fruit in individual one millimetre slices (9)

indicatorNotes.slices: I and MM slice into PERSON, splitting it

annotation.surface: Someone cuts fruit into slices one millimetre thick.
annotation.walkthrough: Slices looks like the noun, thin pieces of fruit; it is a verb, with I MM cutting into PERSON.
annotation.definitionFit: The persimmon is an orange fruit, also called sharon fruit.

entries.clue: Mister Joseph’s eldest brother holding most of deposit back (9)

indicatorNotes.holding: to hold is to contain, so REUBEN holds SIL within its letters
indicatorNotes.back: the whole assembly is read backwards

blocks.note: in Genesis, Reuben is Jacob's firstborn, Joseph's eldest brother
SILT, a river deposit, without its last letter

annotation.surface: A Mr Joseph whose eldest brother keeps back most of a deposit, like a family squabble over money.
annotation.walkthrough: Mister looks like a form of address; it is one who mists, a device that turns liquid into a fine spray.
annotation.definitionFit: A nebuliser turns liquid medicine into a mist to be breathed in, so it is literally a mister.

entries.clue: Doctor’s prime spot by blankets? (7)

indicatorNotes.prime: the prime letter of Doctor is its first
indicatorNotes.blankets: BESIDE blankets D, wrapping round it

annotation.surface: Where a good doctor stands: right by the patient's bed.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition, with the question mark flagging that spot by blankets is a playful way of saying beside the bed.
annotation.definitionFit: A doctor's best place is the bedside, where bedside manner counts.

entries.clue: Professor’s one needing coat (7)

indicatorNotes.Professor’s: a professor professes, declaring out loud, so what follows is heard rather than read

blocks.note: one who lacks something is a lacker

annotation.surface: An academic who needs a coat for the cold.
annotation.walkthrough: Professor looks like an academic; here it is one who professes, declaring things out loud. Coat is the verb or noun for a layer of varnish.
annotation.definitionFit: Lacquer is a hard glossy coating.

entries.clue: Praise movie withdrawing permissive parts (5)

indicatorNotes.withdrawing: to withdraw is to draw back, so LAX is drawn back to front
indicatorNotes.parts: XAL parts E and T, going between them

annotation.surface: A critic praises a film for cutting its racy scenes.
annotation.walkthrough: Permissive parts suggests the steamy scenes of a film; parts is a verb, XAL separating the two letters of ET.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, usually with a religious or lofty flavour: to exalt is to raise up in praise.

entries.clue: Istanbul address set up ID and iron locks in flat (7)

indicatorNotes.set up: in a down clue, set up turns ID and FE upside down
indicatorNotes.locks in: the reversed letters lock FEN inside them

blocks.note: ID + FE, the symbol for iron, read upwards

annotation.surface: Someone in Istanbul sets up their address and ID and brings an iron into their flat.
annotation.walkthrough: Address is a form of address, a title, not a street location; flat is a noun meaning low marshy land, not an apartment.
annotation.definitionFit: Effendi is a Turkish title of respect, like sir, used in addressing a man.

entries.clue: Leading writer owns record collection (7)

blocks.note: arch = chief, leading, as in archbishop
the writer says I have, I've

annotation.surface: A top author owns a collection of vinyl records.
annotation.walkthrough: Record collection suggests music; it is a collection of documents. The writer of a clue refers to themselves as I.
annotation.definitionFit: An archive is a store of documents, so record collection fits in the paperwork sense, not the vinyl one.

entries.clue: Batting failure masking century England’s opener got (7)

indicatorNotes.masking: DUD masks C and E, covering them
indicatorNotes.opener: England's opener is its first letter

blocks.note: a side batting in cricket is in

annotation.surface: A batting collapse is hidden because England's opening batsman scored a hundred.
annotation.walkthrough: The cricket scene makes opener look like the opening batsman and century like a hundred runs; got is a verb, as in got him to agree.
annotation.definitionFit: To get someone to do something is to induce them.

entries.clue: American’s parking in departure area way below (5)

indicatorNotes.in: parking comes in, as a substitute comes in, taking the place of the A

blocks.note: death is a departure from life

annotation.surface: An American parks at an airport's departure area, far below.
annotation.walkthrough: American's parking is short for American has parking in: A is swapped for P. Departure area looks like an airport; departure alone is a euphemism for death.
annotation.definitionFit: The depths are the deepest part of something, an area far below.

entries.clue: Does corrupt criminal court void fines? (7)

indicatorNotes.criminal: criminal = wrong, so the letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.void: COURT emptied of its middle leaves CT

annotation.surface: A question about whether a crooked court cancels the penalties it imposes.
annotation.walkthrough: Does corrupt is an emphatic verb, standing for corrupts; the question mark ends a surface that is really a statement.
annotation.definitionFit: Infection spreads rot as corruption does; does corrupt is just the emphatic form of corrupts.

entries.clue: Plane quiet with just 50 per cent aboard winter flight (3,4)

indicatorNotes.with just 50 per cent: only half of JUST is used, JU
indicatorNotes.aboard: JU goes aboard SKIM, inside it

blocks.note: to plane over water is to skim

annotation.surface: A quiet plane only half full of passengers on a winter flight.
annotation.walkthrough: Plane looks like an aircraft, but it is the verb to skim; the flight is the skier's leap off the ramp.
annotation.definitionFit: A ski jump is a leap through the air on skis, a flight in winter sport.

entries.clue: Large poles separating cereal crop (3-4)

indicatorNotes.separating: N and S go between MA and IZE, separating it

blocks.note: N and S, the north and south poles

annotation.surface: Big posts dividing up a field of cereal.
annotation.walkthrough: Poles looks like fence posts; it is N and S, the two poles of the earth.
annotation.definitionFit: Man-size means large, big enough for a man.

entries.clue: Charge seen in mobile web app (6,6)

indicatorNotes.mobile: mobile = moving, so the letters shift about

annotation.surface: A fee turns up in a phone's web app.
annotation.walkthrough: Mobile sits naturally beside web app as a phone; it is the anagram signal, and seen in is fodder, not a link.
annotation.definitionFit: A search engine is a web application for finding pages.
